fields.statement: Built rhiza at the branch head (7420691c fix included) into a scratch root with fake rex and gh. A command step 'sleep 300' with stall = "5s", started as a session leader (setsid rhiza run start --foreground --autonomous): after 9s rhiza daemon --once logged 'step one silent since ...: stopped and resumed with --retry (budget 1 of 2)', and ps showed both the run and its 'sh -c exec 2>&1 sleep 300' child and sleep gone (cycle 1 left them orphaned). The next poll resumed it as a detached 'rhiza run resume --foreground <run> --retry'; that stalled again and the following poll stopped it, its sleep child gone too (budget 2 of 2). A wait step with timeout = "20s" under rhiza.daemon.watchdog.waitLimit = 5s was left alone past 9s (limit = timeout + 10m) and ended on its own timeout; the same wait step with stall = "5s" was stopped and retried.

Same stalled run, each poll a fresh rhiza daemon --once process: after two stop-and-retry recoveries a third stall got no stop (its step left running for the owner), and rhiza inbox listed one 'stalled run ... step one' item: 'the watchdog's retry budget of 2 is spent ... it tried: step one stalled: stopped and resumed with --retry at <t1>; ... at <t2>'.

The first stall recovery logged 'filed a bug request for the stall' and the next poll started that request's plan run (fake rex, no agent); the second recovery of the same run filed none. A stall on another run (wait step) filed its own bug request.

After the real polls, rhiza health listed 'watchdog's last actions, newest first:' with budget 2 of 2, then budget 1 of 2, then the bug filing, each with its RFC 3339 time, matching the 'rhiza: daemon: watchdog: ...' lines on stderr.

An autonomous run whose command step 'rhiza ship check --settled' failed (fake gh answering pr view with a CLOSED PR) was polled by four rhiza daemon --once processes: the fake gh log showed one 'gh pr view' in total, none on later polls, and no gh run list or rerun (47741152: the PR is read once and a closed PR is not re-read while the journal is unchanged).
